title: Continuous batching scheduler tuning experiments - notes
summary: Live notes from experiments tuning the continuous-batching scheduler. Focus: batch_size, timeout, fairness policies and their impact on p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and GPU utilization. Goal is to find operational sweet spots and heuristics for adaptive timeouts to reduce tail latency without sacrificing throughput.
experiment_plan: 1) Baseline (current prod-like config): max_batch=16, min_batch=1, timeout_ms=10, FIFO fairness. 2) Sweep max_batch in [8,16,32]. 3) Sweep timeout_ms in [2,5,10,20,50]. 4) Compare fairness policies: FIFO, size-weighted (prefer small requests), age-priority, and per-model priority. 5) Synthetic workload (mixed short/long seqs) + replay a sampled subset of production traces. 6) Collect kernel-level traces + runtime metrics for each run.
workload_description: - Mixed traffic: 70% short text-complete requests (avg tokens generated=12), 20% medium (avg=64), 10% long streaming (avg=512). - Two model classes: small open LLaMA-like quantized model (FP16/4-bit) and medium-sized 7B variant. - Request arrival modeled as Poisson with bursts to simulate PLG spikes. - Also replayed 30k requests captured during a weekday spike window for sanity check.
hardware_and_build: - CI cluster nodes: 4x A100 80GB per node (NVLink enabled). - Serving runtime: build v1.14.2 with batching scheduler flags exposed. - CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9.x. - Batching code instrumented with wall-clock timestamps at enqueue/dequeue/dispatch/complete and per-request token emit times. - Profiling with nvprof/nsys for representative runs.
metrics_monitored: Throughput (tokens/s and requests/s), p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end), GPU utilization, GPU SM % active, memory copy times (H2D/D2H), kernel launch overhead, queue occupancy, average batch size, fair-share violation count (requests starved more than 2x expected wait), tail fraction (requests > target_slo).
results_summary: - Increasing max_batch from 16 -> 32 yields ~18-22% throughput uplift for long requests but increases p99 by ~40-70ms for short requests under bursty arrivals. - Tightening timeout_ms from 20 -> 5ms reduces p99 tail for short requests by ~35ms but reduces throughput for long generators (because more small batches are dispatched). - Size-weighted fairness (prefer small requests) drastically improves p99 for short requests (50-60ms improvement) with only ~6% throughput loss on long requests. - Age-priority prevented starvation in extreme cases but increased median latency slightly. - Adaptive timeout (timeout proportional to current queue occupancy and recent arrival rate) achieved a good tradeoff: ~12% throughput hit vs baseline but p99 reduction of ~30-45ms for short requests and minimal impact on long sequences.
detailed_findings: 1) Head-of-line blocking: FIFO with large max_batch causes small requests to wait behind a single long request when it arrives early in the batch window. Evidence: request traces show long requests captured at head and subsequent small requests incur wait equal to remaining long generation time. 2) Kernel vs copy: profiling shows kernel compute dominates for long sequences as expected, but for short sequences kernel launch + memcpy overheads are non-trivial (~12-18% of request time). 3) Timeout tradeoffs: Lowering timeout reduces queueing latency but increases number of small dispatched batches, increasing kernel invocation rate and slight CPU overhead. 4) Fairness policy impact: Size-weighted policy effectively reduces effective wait for small requests by biasing dispatch when queue contains a high fraction of small requests. Implementation note: we used an approximate size bucket classifier on enqueue. 5) Adaptive timeout: Simple heuristic worked well — base_timeout = 5ms, scaled_timeout = base_timeout + alpha * (queue_len / max_batch) where alpha tuned to 20ms. When queue_len near max_batch, scaled_timeout increases so batches fill. This reduced unnecessary early flushes during sustained high load. 6) Tail variance correlates with arrival burstiness and long-sequence fraction; controlling head-of-line blocking is more beneficial than merely lowering max_batch.
profiling_notes: - Use nsys to capture a 30s window for representative run; tag traces with request ids. - Observed spikes of cudaMemcpyAsync queuing delays when many small batches dispatched in short intervals. - Kernel launch latency variance higher when multiple worker threads call into CUDA concurrently; batching gateway serialized calls helps reduce variance. - NVLink reduces H2H overhead between GPUs but not main issue here (single-GPU serving for most tests). - Pay attention to NVTX ranges when correlating request lifecycle to kernels.
recommendations: - Short term (A): enable size-weighted fairness as an opt-in scheduler mode for prod (improves short-request tail with small throughput impact). - Short term (B): set default timeout_ms=5 for request-heavy endpoints and provide override per-route. - Medium term: implement adaptive timeout heuristic based on queue occupancy and measured arrival rate; rollout behind feature flag. - Medium term: expose per-route batching profiles in Console and allow customers to select latency vs throughput preference. - Instrumentation: add queue-occupancy and per-request wait reason tags to telemetry; track fair-share violations and head-of-line incidents. - Long term: consider hybrid scheduler that splits queues by predicted sequence-length class and runs size-aware batch assembly to avoid inter-class head-of-line blocking.
next_steps: 1) Run an A/B with size-weighted fairness on a small percentage of traffic next week (QA sign-off). 2) Implement adaptive timeout feature flag and run load test with production trace replays. 3) Add a CI check that runs microbench for kernel launch overhead when PR touches batching code. 4) Draft Console UI proposal for per-route batching preferences and expose p99 by route. 5) Follow-up: test on Dedicated nodes with multi-GPU sharding to validate NVLink interactions.
notes: - Lots of conversational comments in the raw traces; we should sanitize before any external sharing. - Open questions: best alpha for adaptive timeout across different model families; need cross-model family experiments. - Link to earlier experiments: see continuous-batching-scheduler-tuning-experiments-{1..6} for baseline configs and auxiliary scripts.
